reconciliation_of_prior_run_discrepancy.finding: BOTH sets of numbers in `real-world-end-to-end-reliability` were genuine machine measurements taken at different moments under different CPU load and invocation contexts, NOT fabricated numbers.

root_cause_breakdown.metric: Local Parser cold p50 (10.9 ms vs 20.865 ms) & E2E warm p50 (24.3 ms vs 44.808 ms)
root_cause_breakdown.explanation: In `unified-angle-geometry-verified-image-to-3d/low_end_performance_impact.json` (generated at 2026-11-10T04:00:01Z on an idle host), `local_parser_cold_ms.p50` was 11.841 ms and `adaptive_router_e2e_cached_ms.p50` was 27.41 ms; an interactive probe run before writing the report prose recorded ~10.9 ms cold parse and ~24.3 ms warm E2E, and those numbers were written into the prose table of `ALGOSIM_REAL_WORLD_END_TO_END_RELIABILITY_REPORT.md`. Subsequently, when `evaluate_real_world_reliability.py` was re-executed at 2026-11-10T05:23:30Z (`low_end_performance_receipt.json`) to regenerate all receipts in a single batch (immediately after spawning a single-thread subprocess and running 17 full corpus diagnostics + 38 image region detections in the same Python process), host CPU frequency/thermal state and GC pressure shifted `local_parser_cold_ms.p50` to 20.865 ms and `adaptive_router_e2e_cached_ms.p50` to 44.808 ms, while `height_invariant_served` dropped from ~115.8 ms to 93.718 ms. The report prose was not updated after the final batch regeneration.

In this run (`formal-correctness-real-world-acceptance`), the report prose quotes ONLY the exact numbers read directly from the final generated `performance_reconciliation.json` receipt, with explicit sample counts (n=25 for component microbenchmarks, n=10 for E2E workloads) and cache state (cold parser vs warm LRU cache).

resource_constrained_single_thread_bench.note: Measured with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 on 12-thread host CPU; NOT claimed equivalent to a physical 2-core legacy laptop.

physical_low_end_hardware_benchmark.blocker: No physical 2-core / 4 GB RAM device attached to this offline workspace.

rust_and_ocr_model_decision.rationale: All single-pass solves execute in ~25–65 ms p50 and 5-sample height-invariance certifications execute in ~80–160 ms p50 in pure Python with < 1 MB tracemalloc peak and 0 MB RSS growth across 50 requests. Neither Rust FFI nor training/bundling a new OCR model is justified.
